name: mlflow_artifacts_local_disk
title: MLflow artifacts land on the Airflow worker's local disk; other containers can't load the models

found_by.how: Seen during the reference run (MLflow artifact folder empty), then shown by downloading the best run's model through the MLflow server from the flask-app container.

command: docker compose exec -T flask-app python3 -c "import mlflow; mlflow.set_tracking_uri('http://mlflow:5000'); mlflow.artifacts.download_artifacts('runs:/24ad3ef05ed74e95ad57df47e996a4cf/sklearn-gradient-boosting-regression', dst_path='/tmp/fault5')"
error_tail: mlflow.exceptions.MlflowException: The following failures occurred while downloading one or more artifacts from /tmp/artifacts/1/24ad3ef05ed74e95ad57df47e996a4cf/artifacts:

cause.summary: The artifact root is a plain local path and the MLflow server doesn't serve artifacts
details: mlflow/Dockerfile line 35 starts mlflow server with --default-artifact-root $MLFLOW_DEFAULT_ARTIFACT_ROOT, set to /tmp/artifacts (docker-compose.yaml line 337); no --serve-artifacts / --artifacts-destination.

With a plain local path, each MLflow client writes artifacts to its own filesystem: the Airflow worker writes to its /tmp/artifacts (host ./airflow/mlflow_artifacts, line 48), while the server's /tmp/artifacts (host ./mlflow/artifacts, line 353) stays empty.
Any other container (serving, evaluation) that loads a model by run URI fails. dag_03 works around it by copying the best model to S3 from the worker.

fix.summary: One shared artifact store, served by the MLflow server
fix.action: Start the server with --serve-artifacts and --artifacts-destination s3://mlflow-bucket/... (LocalStack, MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localstack:4566) or a volume mounted only on the server, so clients get mlflow-artifacts:/ URIs.

static_check.rule: the MLflow server's artifact root is a plain local path (not a URI) and the server is not started with --serve-artifacts / --artifacts-destination, while other services log or load models

reproduce.how: Run the pipeline (dag_01, dag_02), then load any run's model through MLflow from a container other than the Airflow worker.
reproduce.command: docker compose exec -T flask-app python3 -c "import mlflow; mlflow.set_tracking_uri('http://mlflow:5000'); mlflow.artifacts.download_artifacts('runs:/<run_id>/<model_name>')"
reproduce.note: Not visible in the project's own flow, because the API loads the model from S3.
